title: A reported file edit fences every carried gate of its session, even when the edited path is outside the gate's worktree or under its scratch directory
outcome: An edit report that names its path (Claude's Write and Edit tools do) fences a carried gate only when that path lies in the gate's worktree and outside its `.tmp/` scratch directory; an edit report with no path keeps today's rule.
acceptance: A test reports an edit by the holder to a path in another worktree, and one under the gate's own `.tmp/`, while its gate runs: the carried check is not fenced and is credited.
A test reports an edit by the holder to a tracked file in the gate's worktree: the carried check is fenced, and the line names the edit.
An edit report that carries no path still fences every carried check of the session whose run is going; a test pins it.
The full gate passed on the exact landed input.
The same placement applies to an edit another session reports; a test covers both directions.
docs/test.md and docs/features/engram-host-adapter.md describe the rule, including what happens for a path Git ignores outside `.tmp/` (such as `target/`).
disposal_reason: Same general scope as w-aa25f77a6d2b: exempting edits outside the carried root (other worktrees' tracked files, other sessions' edits). Per Architect2 ae3eb942, an exemption needs a ProvenOutside verdict; per Architect1 013d287a, that needs a per-operation cwd and a link-exit account; per 8f791136, w-aa25f77a6d2b carries that limitation. The narrow, achievable part (another worktree's .tmp/ scratch, absolute targets, fail-closed) goes to w-7997342bfc0b. Agreed by Fable2 (#1419); the carried root's own .tmp/ stays fenced for now.
